pillars.title: PILLAR 1-CITIZEN PARTICIPATION (Focus - Promote and encourage active citizenry, whistleblowing, integrity, and transparency in all spheres of society.)

outcomes.title: Outcome 1A: Active citizenry empowered through advocacy campaigns on anti-corruption, governance matters; and the negative effects of corruption

indicators.name: Anti-corruption strategy launched via a broad-based multi-sectoral event
Increased reach and engagement across diverse communication channels.
Percentage increase in public adherence to the promoted values as evidenced by surveys or behavioural observations.
Improved perception and trust levels of citizens towards the targeted values.
Increased empowerment and exercise of citizens' rights within targeted populations.
indicators.responsible:
Implementing agencies
NGOs or CSOs conducting awareness programs
Government departments involved in citizen rights education

indicators.name: Increase utilisation of legal resources and reporting of rights violations among the citizenry.
Percentage increase in the number of sustained collaborative efforts or projects led by CSOs, educational institutions, or community groups post-partnership establishment.
Percentage increase in the adoption of ethical behaviour and demonstration of knowledge about citizens' rights among students in schools where campaigns have been integrated into the curriculum.

Percentage increase in students' active engagement in promoting ethical behaviour and advocating for citizens' rights, as evidenced by their participation in related activities or initiatives within and outside the school environment.
Increased collaboration and commitment to anti-corruption efforts among stakeholders as evidenced by policy changes or enforcement actions.
Percentage increase in public trust in government institutions and perceived transparency in decision-making processes, as measured by surveys or polls conducted after public dialogues.

outcomes.title: Outcome 1B: All stakeholders, across all sectors of society, work together towards a common goal of preventing and combating corruption within their spheres of influence; and people willingly report corruption because they understand the benefits of doing and whistleblowers feel protected and supported.

indicators.name: Informed decision-making and strategic planning for the establishment of the central reporting agency.
Efficient allocation and utilisation of resources for the successful implementation of the central reporting agency.
indicators.responsible: Oversight bodies or government agencies monitoring the project

indicators.name: Prompt and effective implementation of the central reporting mechanism.
Improved accountability and responsiveness in addressing reported cases.

Percentage increase in the number of whistleblower reports where recommendations are implemented within the specified timeframe, resulting in demonstrable improvements in organizational processes, practices, or outcomes.
Improved organizational culture and support for whistleblowing.
Enhanced transparency and accountability in organizational practices.
Percentage increase in the number of employees who report feeling confident in their ability to identify and report misconduct, as evidenced by post-training surveys or assessments.
Enhanced trust in the confidentiality and fairness of the whistleblowing process, as measured through employee satisfaction surveys or feedback mechanisms.

outcomes.title: Outcome 1C: Increased public participation and discourse on ethical conduct and a shift in the national consciousness towards societal reorientation to a values-based way of life evident in communities, workplaces, schools, higher education institutions and other civil society structures.

indicators.name: Enhanced ethical awareness and behaviour among students.
Strengthened commitment to ethical education and values among students and institutions.
Improved organisational culture and commitment to ethical conduct.
indicators.responsible: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition

indicators.name: Enhanced awareness and understanding of ethical standards among employees.
Strengthened media freedom and independence, fostering a more robust and pluralistic democratic society.
An enhanced media landscape that promotes investigative journalism and reporting on anti-corruption.
Percentage decrease in instances of ethical misconduct or corruption within sectors with established committees or forums
Enhanced capacity and commitment to ethical conduct among key stakeholders.
Percentage decrease in the average time taken to resolve reported corruption cases within sectors with established committees

outcomes.title: Outcome 1D: Greater transparency and improved measures for providing access to information in all sectors, in particular about governance, that is, business, CSOs and political parties.

indicators.name: Enhanced transparency and accessibility of information within organizations as a result of PAIA.
Increase in instances where information obtained through PAIA requests has led to positive changes, such as increased public scrutiny, or accountability measures.
Enhanced efficiency and effectiveness of administrative processes.
indicators.responsible: PAIA Compliance Officers, oversight bodies, Department of Justice, and Constitutional Development

indicators.name: Increased confidence in administrative processes and compliance with regulations.
Improved oversight functions supported by digitised administrative systems and enhanced data integrity management.
Increase in corruption investigations or prosecutions facilitated by access to accurate and comprehensive beneficial ownership information.
Increase in the percentage of companies or entities that comply with beneficial ownership disclosure requirements over time.

Improve transparency in governance through professional guidelines, information campaigns and communication on successes, e.g. arrests/
convictions, and the consequences of corruption
Adoption and implementation of reporting mechanisms in private sector organisations
Improved reporting culture and transparency in the private sector
Improvement in the satisfaction and confidence levels of whistleblowers with the support mechanisms provided by their organisations.
Enhanced Transparency in Political Party Funding through disclosures
Strengthened regulatory framework for political party funding transparency
